text_fidelity_a:
Gatorade Stainless Steel Sport Bottle, 26oz, Double-Wall Insulation I drink out of insulated stainless cups frequently, mostly tumblers or thermos-style, so I was interested to try this new Gatorade insulated stainless sports bottle.

I really love the lid they designed for this, it is super easy to drink from any angle unlike yeti tumblers where it can leak if the opening isn't aligned with your mouth perfectly, and it is also capable of higher flow than most other stainless cup lids which is great if you are really thirsty after working out. I also like that the cup is dishwasher safe, unlike most stainless cups which recommend hand washing.. and the lid is very easy to clean also and doesn't seem prone to collecting mold even when used with sugary drinks. Some other reviewers have complained about the lid leaking but in my experience it is really easy to prevent as long as you make sure to close it all the way, which isn't difficult.

The only thing I really don't care for about this bottle is the loud branding, even though Gatorade is a brand which I like, I don't enjoy feeling like a walking advertisement and it also makes the bottle seem a little out of place when used in a non-sports setting. That said, I like the lid design on this bottle so much that my other stainless cups have been collecting dust since I got this one.
text_fidelity_b: Gatorade Stainless Steel Sport Bottle, 26oz, Double-Wall Insulation

text_fidelity_a:
SPRI Stash It Belt One of the most frustrating things for me is if I want to go for a long walk in a rural area and I have to have a phone near by. I prefer to walk without a phone and such, but at times I can not escape the need to have a phone for an important phone call. I really don't like a fanny pack, as it is really big, but was looking for something handier.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This stash belt is very thin. It is deceiving, however. The belt itself is a good quality stretchy elastic. It is heavy duty but not so heavy that it is bulky. There is a black clip in the back, and a slide to make the belt longer or shorter. The pack itself is 2 inches by 9 inches. However, it has a pleat in the top and bottom which make it bigger.

There is a water resistant lining in the pack, a front zipper, and a very thin reflective strip on the front. At full length, the belt measures 34 inches unstretched, and 41 inches stretched. The shortest is 24 inches stretching to about 32 inches.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
When using this, I can put my smart phone into the pack, a set of keys and a few cards. I can also stick in a tissue or two folded small. A huge set of keys will make it a bit tight, but a reasonable ring of keys with several keys on it should be fine. The pack does stretch a little bit so that things will fit.

As far as use, I found that this is very handy. I have to stretch it a little tight so that it does not bobble around as I walk. That is okay though, because it holds it in place. Otherwise, the phone and things can make it sag a little bit. Finding the right tightness takes a bit of trial and error. I really appreciate having this as it makes it the closet to walking without anything that I have been able to get.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I really like this stash belt. It is handy, useful, and makes it so that I can go for long walks without bulky bags or packs. Safe and with decent capacity, I can carry what I want to have with me yet feel free and lightweight at the same time. With a range of sizes it will fit, many people would benefit from this, but if you are a big and tall man, it might be a bit tight.

RATING
Five stars for this. I really like it. It is handy and easy to use. I will update if I have anything else important to add in the future.
text_fidelity_b: SPRI Stash It Belt

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in)) I want so badly to give this 5-stars. I am settling with 3 for now. Here's why:
Pros-
This is my first fitness tracker. I like that it measures my heart beat and steps- the exercise mode is nice too. I LOVE that I can sync it with my phone to have a vibrated notification of calls/caller ID and that it also does silent alarms. These features have been quickly integrated into my daily routine and I LOVE them!

Cons-
My first complaint comes about the mobile app. I have an android phone. My son has the CHARGE fitbit, and for some reason his app tells how long it takes him to fall asleep (minor difference, I will admit, but...) the app, while displaying the stats info from your tracker, as well as compiling averages for periods of time, doesn't give suggestions on how to modify your routine. The website offers a "premium" service, which gives you more detailed analysis, but I'm not sure it will also provide those missing helpful suggestions.
My second, and biggest complaint is the battery. I saw one reviewer experienced a similar issue with their fitbit and I can say after a mere 9 days of use, I can barely go 24hrs without a low battery notice, it's going back. I have been in touch with fitbit customer support today, and they seem to.be on top of things, but if I don't get a response I'm happy with, I'll have to try something else. My son has a refurbished fitbit charge, and it is working VERY well. I wanted us to be able to continue to run challenges ( he's 9, so keeping up with his 12,000 steps a day is an EXCELLENT GOAL for me!) But if I have to switch brands, I guess I will. Will update this review as soon as something changes!

Update! 11 months later:
I am so disappointed with my entire fitbit experience. I purchased another HR finding a better deal elsewhere after my original band quit working on me and I returned it to amazon. I should have quit while I was ahead. I have had 3 replacements, first 2 had issues with the internal functions and quit working. The 3rd fell apart. I do not wear in the shower, avoid getting it wet, or leaving damp after sweating even a little. I finally gave up and asked fitbit to do something- their response, I could have ANOTHER charge hr OR throw away my original $$$ and purchase ANOTHER Fitbit product at 30% off. Seriously?! I didn't have any of the trackers for more than 4 months each and they wanted me to replace their failed product by PAYING MORE for a replacement. No way! Throughly disgusted. Please, if you don't have disposable income to keep paying to replace these, look elsewhere.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge HR Wireless Activity Wristband (Tangerine, Large (6.2 - 7.6 in))

Slant Board - Multi-Level Slanted Calf Stretcher - Adjustable Wooden Incline Exercise Platform - Perfect for Tight Muscles, Plantar Fasciitis, Achilles Tendonitis - Supports Up to 350lbs weight I have been using the thick ream of printer paper to do regular bunion exercises in my doorway for some time now. The problem is that when I need to use the paper, there goes my lift. Books don't tend to work as well for me, but then I saw this. YAY! It is PERFECT!

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This amazing little unit is fabulous. It comes all folded up and has a heavy duty carry case in it. There are pieces that need to be put on it. I will break it down for you.

HEEL REST
There are two heel rests that go on the bottom of the foot board if you want to use them. They have four pegs which tightly fit into the wood holes drilled for them. There are two screw holes to keep them in place, along with screws that come with the unit. YOU WILL HAVE TO USE A POWER DRILL TO PUT THE SCREWS IN. IT IS NOT PRE-DRILLED INTO THE WOOD BASE PART.

FOOT REST
The place where you put your feet has like heavy duty sandpaper on it. That will hold feet in place either with shoes or bare feet. I have no problems using this with bare feet which I prefer.

EYE PINS
There are several levels that you can put the incline at, and two eye pins that you simply slip through the holes once they are set at level to keep it in place.

LEVELS
The levels of this are PERFECT for me. They are great to put centered in a doorway. Using the sides of the door frame, I tilt backwards and then slowly pull myself upright parallel with the door frame and hold in place for about 30 seconds if I can and then slowly let myself go backwards again.

Several repetitions at level 2 and I am ready to move up again.

DOES IT HELP?
This is fabulous. It is perfect. It helps and does exactly what I want it to. My calves are stretched and it does help keep bunions reduced with consistent use.

DOES IT HOLD WEIGHT?
We have a variety of weights in the family up to 300 lbs. Everyone felt very sturdy on this, although the largest one does not like calf stretches, so they won't be using it. Heck, NO ONE will be using this because I want it to stay in one piece. HAHA Guess I will have to hide this too.

CASE
The case makes it much easier to use this board. It has handles, and zips shut. The fabric is very sturdy and will hold up for quite a while. I love it because I can put it away and bring it out easier due to the handles.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I am VERY happy with this board. It has helped me resume my bunion stretches so I don't have to depend on reams of printer paper anymore. I can pull this out anytime I want and be able to use this in my doorway, barefoot or with shoes on.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is just what I wanted. It is perfect for me. HIGHLY recommended.
text_fidelity_b: Slant Board - Multi-Level Slanted Calf Stretcher - Adjustable Wooden Incline Exercise Platform - Perfect for Tight Muscles, Plantar Fasciitis, Achilles Tendonitis - Supports Up to 350lbs weight

This comes with a zipper and an extra pull included. I can see why. This zipper is quite difficult to use. The pack includes a lubrication tube and tells you how to keep the zipper working. Well, I did it several times and it still is not easy to slide the zipper.

The inside is quite a bit smaller than the outside due to the insulation. Our milk bottles will only fit long ways instead of sideways as I thought they would.

DOES IT KEEP THINGS COLD?
I have to say that I got some yogurt the other day and did not have ice to put in the cooler. I put in 3 containers of yogurt which were quart sized. I had them in there for about 5 hours. When I got home, the yogurt was still pretty cold. I am impressed.

STRAPS/HANDLE
The straps and handle on this cooler are really great. The shoulder strap makes it easy for me to carry this along with the other things I have to carry in the house It is comfortable and works out well.

LEAKS?
This did not leak so far when ice melts.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is the perfect cooler for getting our milk this summer. It will allow me to make the trip and not be so concerned about keeping the milk cold in our other coolers because this one with some ice included will work perfectly.

text_fidelity_a:
Square36 Extra Large Exercise Mat 8' x 6' x 7mm Thick. Heavy Duty Gym Mats for Home Workouts Non-Toxic, Non-Slip, For Use With or Without Shoes Exercise Mat - Cardio Workout Mats for Home Gym Flooring. My husband purchased this for me as a Christmas gift to use in my (finished) basement exercise room. We had been wanting to get something to protect our Berber-style carpet and had looked into options such as puzzle mats, but everything seemed to have drawbacks. My sweet husband found this on his own after careful research. He knew that as a yoga teacher, I would want something non-slip for yoga and/or that I could place a yoga mat on top if needed. However, he also knew that I use my exercise room for strength and cardio workouts as well, and so he wanted a mat that would be safe to walk on with workout shoes.

This Square36 Mat fits all of the above criteria! For yoga, it is as non-slip as my best (Manduka) yoga mat. At first, I was still laying down my regular yoga mat over top the Square36 for practicing yoga, but now, I don't usually bother. Because I have the Extra Large size (8 x 6-Feet), I can comfortably practice in any direction I want, which is wonderful! Now that I'm in my late 40s, I love how the mat provides a bit of extra cushion for cardio workouts. (One note: I am a little careful performing pivoting maneuvers on the mat.) As with yoga, I really appreciate that I can perform cardio routines all over the mat, moving in 360-degrees. Finally, the mat is perfect for strength workouts as well. I can place weights--even heavy kettlebells--on the mat without fear of damaging it.

I did not experience any smell with this mat when it was new, and it flattened out easily once I laid it out. On my flat carpet, it does shift a little. There is no actual movement when I am using the mat, but about once a month, I notice that it has moved back maybe 2-3"; it is easy enough to slide it back into its original position. I've now had the mat for six months, and it still looks as good as when I first got it. The only real care I give it is occasional vacuuming (although I might also wipe it down once and awhile with a damp cloth if something seems to have gotten on it). Overall, I think the Square36 is a very good, versatile mat that I would recommend for the exercise enthusiast.
text_fidelity_b: Square36 Extra Large Exercise Mat 8' x 6' x 7mm Thick. Heavy Duty Gym Mats for Home Workouts Non-Toxic, Non-Slip, For Use With or Without Shoes Exercise Mat - Cardio Workout Mats for Home Gym Flooring.

Timex Ironman Run Trainer GPS with Heart Rate This is my first GPS running watch. So I have limited comparison experience.
I have been running for about 30 years now. For many of those years I have used a Polar heart rate monitor. When I saw the GPS watches, I thought they might be useful to monitor my runs in unfamiliar territory. I figured I could run a set distance even on vacation.
This watch can do that, and more. It measures distance, time and heartrate, but it also links to a website that maps the run and tracks elevation and calories burned. I am enjoying this very, very much.
I gave it four stars, not five, because it sometimes takes a few minutes to pick up the satellites. In all honesty, I don't know firsthand how that compares to other GPS watches, but reading about them it seems some take longer but some less time.
Another great thing about this watch is the transmitter. It is a standard chest transmitter that can work with other brand watches as well.
All in all, a great device at a very good price.
I'm pleased with the value.
text_fidelity_b: Timex Ironman Run Trainer GPS with Heart Rate

Weaver Leather Original Adjustable Nylon Horse Halter I bought one of these 3 years ago and it stood up well, after the first year the lime green color was faded but it still washed up and held up nicely with good stitching and hardware. After about 1.5 years the chin strap clip got bent and didn't close until I hammered it back into place more. It was iffy and had to get whacked several times for over a year and a half but it wasn't until a few days ago that it finally broke during a touch up hammering. Amazon's price currently beat the online horse supply stores I had previously purchased from and I went with graphite and french blue colors and they are really nice.

My horse is pasture boarded so he doesn't wear a halter unless I'm doing something with him, but during the warmer months I honestly just hang his halter and lead on a tree branch or hook on the fence out in the sun/rain/elements. 3 years of abuse and the only wear was color fade and a clip broken from being constantly beaten is a good longevity in my book. If he had to wear a halter full time I would have gotten a single-layer nylon adjustable halter with just rings instead of these very heavy D-shaped rings, just so he'd have something lighter.

My horse is a 16h 1000-1100 quarter horse with a proportional but more warmblood-looking than QH-looking head and the large horse size fits perfectly on the smaller holes for the behind the ears strap and the middle size holes for the around the nose strap.
text_fidelity_b: Weaver Leather Original Adjustable Nylon Horse Halter

The unit fell apart primary due to the fact they are too cheap to use Loctite or equivalent to secure screws--only the brake unit had Loctite.

- month one the handle bar screws needed to be tightened every week
- month two the knob on the rear wheel cover which the neck lock to carry fell off
- month two the neck screw had to be tightened weekly
- month three brake needed to be adjusted--not a big deal, but..
- month four the neck screw' nut fell off and I could not find a replacement at Homedepot

Customer service was slow and they insisted I shipped the entire unit for warranty service. Why would I be expected to ship the entire unit back to have screws or other small parts easily replaceable by the customer?

I tossed the scooter in a corner in the garage so I can responsibly dispose of the battery, later, before tossing it in the trash.

Do yourself a favor and look at Xootr. Quality scooters that will last for ten years or more. They provide parts. It is NOT electric, however.

Spend you money elsewhere for these guys do not stand behind their product and have horrible customer service. I feel ripped off! Can you tell?

Gear Doctors Camping Pads Self Inflating Ultralight Apollo air 4.3-5.2 R Insulated Camping mats 1.5-3.3 in Must Haves Inflatable Foam air Sleep mat self Inflating air Mattress for Camping cot I bought these for my family to be able to go camping and have some additional padding under our sleeping bags, as well as to insulate from the ground temperature. While we haven't had opportunity to camp with them yet, I have tested the product out in the house.

At first, I wasn't sure about the inflation, but being inexperienced with this type of product, I really didn't know what to expect (would it inflate like an air mattress, or would inflation be minimal?). When I first unrolled it, it didn't seem to inflate, even after the 3-5 minutes described in the instructions. Then I realized I unrolled it with the valve closed, and the instructions state to unroll with the valve open. So, I rolled it back, squeezing out what air had entered it, then proceeded to unroll again with the valve open. After several minutes, I came back, put it on the floor and tested it. It had inflated significantly more (don't expect an air mattress), though still remained thin. For me it was fairly comfortable on its own, and with my sleeping bag on top of it, it was more than comfortable enough for camping.

After testing it for comfort on the hard floor in my house, I rolled it back up, and a lot of air came out. It was easy to roll and easily went back into its carry bag, which is a big plus (too many products never fit back in their original packaging).

So, short of knowing how it would do on the ground outside in cold weather, I'd say this product was worth the purchase. It seems to be made of high-quality material, and it provides added comfort for sleeping in a sleeping bag.
text_fidelity_b: Gear Doctors Camping Pads Self Inflating Ultralight Apollo air 4.3-5.2 R Insulated Camping mats 1.5-3.3 in Must Haves Inflatable Foam air Sleep mat self Inflating air Mattress for Camping cot

text_fidelity_a:
Nathan Unisex Hydration Back-Pack for Running, Hiking, Cycling and more. 2L Bladder Included / 6L Storage Capacity. Adjustable Straps. NO BOUNCE while Running. I purchased this vest 6 years ago and it served me well in multiple ultras. It has just enough space for everything you need. I just checked the front zip pocket and it's just a tad too small for my Samsung Galaxy S7 Active, which is a thick phone. It definitely wouldn't fit an iPhone 6-7 Plus. The pack rides low enough on your back that there are no real issues with rubbing or chafing of the neck...from the pack. I did get a bit annoyed from time to time by the hose rubbing my neck, though. The side straps....what can I say? Over 6 years, I've never figured out how to adjust them well, lol. But it hasn't seemed to matter much. For a while, I used to over-cinch the chest strap but realized it can stay pretty loose and the pack is still not very bouncy. The front right pocket is where I've always tucked my phone. Although I admit sometimes I've used a SpiBelt with this pack to free up more pocket space for gels. You don't get a whole lot of space in the back pocket but it's perfect for those rarely used but "just in case" items I like to bring like an emergency poncho, extra sunscreen, lip balm, ginger chews, etc.

The bite valve on Nathan's bladder tube has always been problematic for me. I never really "bit" it hard yet within a year or so, it began to leak. After one race, my leg was covered in syrupy goo where gatorade and leaked and evaporated over the course of 50 miles. I swapped it out for the bite valve from a Camelbak and never had another problem. Like all bladders, be religious about cleaning this one post-use or it will gunk up very quickly. The closure system on the bladder takes some getting use to. You'll become a pro at it but for years I watched aid station volunteers stare in bewilderment, trying to figure out how to open it. More often than not, I ended up doing it myself.

I used to find after 100 milers that the top of my back would have a slightly chaffed feel to it, without anything being rubbed raw. I'm sure a light application of body glide or vasoline would have prevented that. But overall, this is a great, basic vest with plenty of fluid capacity. I recently replaced mine with Nathan's VaporAir, mainly for more pockets. But I could easily have bought this again and been happy.
text_fidelity_b: Nathan Unisex Hydration Back-Pack for Running, Hiking, Cycling and more. 2L Bladder Included / 6L Storage Capacity. Adjustable Straps. NO BOUNCE while Running.

KOR ONE BPA Free Clear Reusable Water Bottle I 750mL I 25 Oz I Sustainable & Eco-Friendly I Leak Proof I One Click Cap w/ Handle I Wide Mouth I Great for Travel & Workouts (Warm Charcoal, 750 ml) I recently bought a kor one bottle. This bottle is decent. One really good feature is the opening- it isn't huge like the ones you find on Nalgene bottles that are just too big. At the same time, the opening, the opening is still big enough to easily fit ice cubes and bottle brushes. The cap/hinge is also interesting. I love that kor does offer replacement gaskets in case yours get worn out, lost, or broken.

The design is really interesting to look at and people notice my bottle all the time. Unfortunately, the unique shape means that I cannot fit my bottle into my standard cup holders in my car. Also, the bottle, because it is an oval makes it taller than most water bottles. This makes it a little cumbersome when travelling.

The lid has a strudy feeling carry handle. You could easily get away with holding this bottle by only the lid. I have read previous reviews that the lid hinge is easily breakable, but I am happy to report that I haven't had that problem with mine under normal use- which includes it falling off the passenger seat of my car almost daily.

Because the plastic is smooth, I have noticed that I have a few scratches on it that are starting to show.

OVERALL: I am happy with this bottle.
-It has a unique look that people admire.
-The opening is not too big or small for drinking, ice, and cleaning.
-The lid seems sturdy enough to withstand regular use.
-Replacement gasket seals are easy to get.
-It DOESN'T fit in cup holders, but is water tight when closed correctly.
text_fidelity_b: KOR ONE BPA Free Clear Reusable Water Bottle I 750mL I 25 Oz I Sustainable & Eco-Friendly I Leak Proof I One Click Cap w/ Handle I Wide Mouth I Great for Travel & Workouts (Warm Charcoal, 750 ml)

Gaiam Walking Fit Kit Pedometer Plus Audio CD (Entry Level) I was very excited to get this, and it was fairly easy to set up, even if the directions are not clear. The door that covers the display is made of plastic, not very sturdy, and the door piece is what you use to clip it on your clothing. I'm amazed it hasn't broken, but so far is doing good....I was sure it would break but so far has not.
I never used the CD that came with it, so I cannot review that.
As far as the functions, it is very easy to see the readout and track your distance in kilometers, miles, and steps traveled.
My only real beef with this is the lack of distance traveled accuracy. Even on it's least sensitive setting, it still adds 1/4 more distance then what I actually traveled. Oddly though, it measures steps correctly when walking on carpeting or on an elliptical. At the track and on cement, plan on shaving off 1/4 of your distance to be semi accurate.
If you want to be encouraged by an overzealous pedometer, go for it. It's easy to use, and fairly comfortable.
If you want perfect accuracy, buy something else.

Now for what I like a lot about this sealskin drape. Made in USA. The drape is thick enough, but not so thick as to be heavy or awkward to deal handle. The material is obviously durable! Whatever it is, it is neither crinkly nor the plastic of any tarp; that is, it won’t split or crack any time soon. Plenty of bungees to help conform the drape to the kayak. Bungees are permanently attached on one side; wrap them under your boat and secure with a sturdy clip to a sturdy eyelet on the opposite side. Excess bungee can be pulled through a locking mechanism on each line to get a snug fit.
If I knew then what I know now, would I still buy the seal skin drape? 100% yes.

I also like that they put a bit of thought in the design, as yes, it is silver, but the back housing (where the laser is) has a black top which minimizes glare - smart. So if someone had said - $20 and you got your self a keeper, I'd've said, ur kidding!

In doing my research for a worthy substitute, I was really attracted to this water bottle. I loved the company's sustainable values and how well-made their product seemed.

When I received the water bottle, I was surprised how lightweight on it is on its own; of course, it gets heavy when you fill it with 40 oz of water, which I wish that I had the foresight to realize before I made this purchase. It is so heavy and wide that I need to use two hands to pick up and drink out of when it is full. The other noticeable thing about the bottle is its beautiful color. I bought it in aqua and it is so eye-catching that I got two compliments on it in my small office during its first day of use.

I did not like the style of the cap which the water bottle came with, so after doing research, I purchased another brand's water bottle cap which was HydroFlask-compatible, which I also thought should be compatible with this one. Unfortunately, it is not. The cap screws on, but it leaks. Of course, this is not the fault of the brand or the water bottle, but it was disappointing to me, and if you are considering buying the bottle and swapping out the cap, this might be worth taking note of.

When I first bought this water bottle, I intended to use it all the time to replace my current water bottle. However, due to its hefty size and weight, I have decided to keep this bottle strictly at the office, as it is even too heavy and unwieldy to bring back and forth to my car, gym, and/or home. I drive a little sedan and it does not fit in my cup holders. I might be bringing it to the gym on my heavy cardio evenings, but it definitely staying in the office for pilates and barre. And it is definitely useful to have around for camping or hiking!

Overall great water bottle and very pleased with the product; unsure how practical it is for daily hydration use when commuting (unless you commute with a backpack).
text_fidelity_b: 45 Degree Latitude 40 oz Water Bottle - Stay Hydrated Camping, Gym, Office Or Sports No BPA Stainless Steel Bottle - Perfectly Ice Cold Or Hot Beverages Leak Proof Lid - Perfect Gift - Celeste Green

Ibagbar Large Vintage Durable Canvas Tote Luggage Weekend Duffel Bag Messenger Shoulder Bag Outdoor Sports Gym Travel Weekend Bag for Men and Women Brown This vintage style canvas bag strikes me as more of a briefcase style laptop bag than any of the other descriptions listed above. I think it would work very well for a teacher, college professor, or a graduate student to use to carry a small laptop, a tablet, folders and papers in. This bag might also be perfect for realtors or insurance salesmen, and it's a nice size to use as a carry on bag when travelling as well.

Measuring 17.7" long x 12.6" high x 7.9" wide, this bag is made of sturdy water resistant canvas with genuine leather trim and stainless steel hardware. The bag has webbed leather trimmed carry handles plus a detachable adjustable strap so it can be carried by hand, as a shoulder bag, or cross body. The brown bag's color is true to the picture shown in the product description and the leather trim, handles, carry strap, and interior lining are done in a darker brown color that provides an attractive contrast.

While most of the bag's storage area is within the roomy main compartment, there are also several storage areas on the outside as well. The front and back of the bag each has a 14" long by 8.5" high zippered compartment which is plenty large enough to carry travel papers, small tablets, or other gear you want ready access to, and there are large 6.5" x 6.5" snap closing sleeves on each end of the bag to hold beverages or other gear.

The zippered main compartment is fully lined in a dark cocoa brown colored cotton fabric which will conceal ink marks or other stains nicely. One side of the compartment has an 8" x 5" zippered compartment, and the other has a well padded 15" long laptop sleeve. I tried to fit my 15" Lenovo Thinkpad into the sleeve but it was too tight, so I think you'll be fine with a 13" or 14" laptop but not a larger one. The laptop did fit into the main compartment itself with room to spare, so you could always use the padded sleeve for a tablet and still take your laptop along.

Stitching throughout this bag is straight and even, and everything is reinforced at stress points. Zippers are well sewn in and all open and closed smoothly. This is a very well made bag made of durable materials. As it can fit everything from a 15" laptop in the center plus folders, or a 14" laptop plus iPad in addition to some books and folders in the center, I think this would make a sturdy book bag, briefcase bag, or travel bag.

This vintage style canvas bag was provided at no cost for evaluation and review.

text_fidelity_a:
Lighting EVER 3300002 1000LM Battery Powered LED Camping Lantern, Waterproof Tent Light, Portable Lantern Flashlight for Hurricane Emergency Purchased this Lighting Ever 1000 lumens lantern and the Rayovac Sportsman 240 Lumen LED Lantern SE3DLNACOM on the same order. Not realizing the identical nature of each lantern at the time, having both in hand together allowed me to make a side by side comparison. This might help someone chose which one to buy.

The Rayovac I purchased on this page shows a 240 lumen lantern, however the one that arrived clearly states 305 lumens. Physically, the LE and RV are manufactured almost identically in composition. Both require 3 D sized batteries to operate. The LE is only one ounce more than the RV, but the LE feels and looks sturdier and of higher quality. LE and RV will be used when describing each lantern, but keep in mind that I am comparing the Rayovac 305 lumen that arrived, versus what is advertised on the Amazon page.

The LE's output on highest mode is 1000 lumens compared to the RV's highest mode at 305; both are daylight white on high. On high, the LE touts a run time of 18 hours (10 watts), to the RV's 70 hours (4 watts), RV wins on run time.

The LE's second mode both reduces the lumens (dimmer) and changes the color temp to a warm white. While the RV does not have a color temp variable, it does provide an option to dim the output to 140 lumens for its 2nd mode and can run 140 hours. LE wins due to the option to change to preferred temperature color.

The LE's 18 hour operation will increase to 25 hours when on mode 2 (warm white). The third mode of the LE further dims the light and combines the warm and daylight temperatures to somewhere in between. The paperwork for the LE shows that mode 3 will last only 12 hours, which does not make sense as to why it shortens the life by the most .

The last mode for both (LE's 4th mode, RVs 3rd mode) is a blinking / strobe light of the daylight / cool white color. I've not much to say on this mode - does not seem relevant at the moment to me. The RV has one final feature though, which is a dim green light on the power button that blinks very slowly, to assist the owner in locating it during periods of darkness. Personally, I do not like this feature and would either remove the batteries or put a dimmit over the light. Buyers might prefer this, I'm just not a fan of idiot lights with or without power.

Lastly, I mentioned these being cut from the same mold, and both have battery compartments in the base of the lantern. The LE has a stem mounted in the base that the cover's slot must align correctly to close the battery compartment. The RV has a slot (no stem) on the rim of base to align to the cover's slot opening. However, the LE cover is still much easier to close with the batteries in the unit. Once the appropriate alignment is met, you must push down and turn to close the base. Think of pushing a child-proof pill bottle's lid to open it. Do the same on these lanterns. The LE base closed after 3 tries, to the RV's numerous tries getting frustrated. LE wins on battery replacement procedures.

Overall, the LE wins hands down. For a 15 ounce lantern with more features, I paid approximately 17.00. The 14 ounce RV cost $24, but the Amazon page shows the list price at $34 and the buyer was getting a $10 discount at purchase. Though the 4 watt RV runs much longer at 2.9 days or 5.8 on mode 2 and the 10 watt LE has a run time of .75 days or 1 full day on mode 2, I am not using this to go camping. This was purchased for power failures, to be used as part of an overall emergency preparedness plan, and bright is what we need indoors during power failures. The hours will be broken up over various times and 18 hours will get us several days. For the money, same battery requirements and functionality, LE takes the cake.

I've never heard of Lighting Ever before, but the product packaging shows they have their home base in Las Vegas, NV, another in the UK and one in China, where this lamp was made. It comes with RoHS certification, 1 year warranty and the instructions are the most accurate regarding the English language than I've seen in a long time. How refreshing to receive grammatically correct documents included in the box (yes, a real box). The RayOVac has a limited lifetime warranty and came in a plastic transparent bag, unbranded. The TLC shows on the LE, while the product packing on the RV is a wrapped label with specs, and it is though product presentation was an afterthought. For the $24, some type of protection during delivery wouldn't hurt. Whoever LE is, I will buy again if they produce a product as good as this one.
text_fidelity_b: Lighting EVER 3300002 1000LM Battery Powered LED Camping Lantern, Waterproof Tent Light, Portable Lantern Flashlight for Hurricane Emergency

text_fidelity_a:
KUBEY KU085 Tactical Folding Knife G10 Handle Stainless Steel Blade Bearing Flipper Hunting Pocket Camping Survival Outdoor Knife (#KU087) Nice knife, especially at this price point. BUT, there are some issues. To me it appeared that this this knife is inferred as being spring assisted. It is most definitely not spring assisted as all other knives are determined to be. The thumb hole is difficult for me to use in one smooth motion. I thought that surely the flipper would be spring assisted, but no. It takes it to half open and no more. You need to use a wrist flip or two hands to finish the opening. That would not be much of a problem, but that makes it illegal to carry here in central Ohio. Sad.

One last thing. This blade is nowhere near 4 inches. It is measured at 3.5 inches. How does Kubey justify these irregularities? Perhaps this is just something being lost in translation.

This knife is super sharp. Locks up like a vault. No wobbles anywhere. It handles well. And it is beautiful. It is definitely worth the money as long as you know up front what you are buying. The build quality is there. The cosmetics are there. It doesn't need this type of advertising to sell. Thus the four stars. I would buy again and I will probably buy from Kubey again.

UPDATE 78/1/17:

The screws holding the clip have become loose. I am in the process of buying a torx bit set so I can tighten them. I wish that this clip could be switched for tip up carry, but the clip orientation cannot be changed.

I have recently discovered that this knife's mode of opening does not make it illegal to carry in Ohio since it requires manually beginning the opening sequence by putting pressure on the blade. Ohio laws are very ambiguous as to what is or is not legal to carry. Happy camper here.
text_fidelity_b: KUBEY KU085 Tactical Folding Knife G10 Handle Stainless Steel Blade Bearing Flipper Hunting Pocket Camping Survival Outdoor Knife (#KU087)

RAYPOSE Womens Workout Capri Leggings for Women with Pockets Plus Size Capris Casual Summer Yoga Pants Women The Raypose High Waist Tummy Control Capri Yoga Pants have side mesh panels, pockets, and a unique fit. More about that later.

The material is dense, not see-through, and has a slight patina that is neither shiny or matte. I would call it more of a slight sheen.

The two mesh panels run the entire length of the outer legs and are only slightly see-through until you reach the pockets, which are lined, so your underwear will not be visible.

The pockets are only 3 1/2" wide and could not accommodate my XS Max, but may fit a smaller phone.

II received these leggings in size medium, but the fit is unlike any size medium I have tried before. I am 5'3", 116 lbs and wear a size small in bottoms, but I review size medium leggings all the time, and I am familiar with how it should fit my body.

When a size medium runs small, it will fit me at the crotch, and when it runs true to size, there is some bunching of excess fabric.

These do not even reach my crotch. I've never experienced that before. It reminded me of 60s style stretch pants with stirrups because the tight calves pulled the legs down and made them straight and taught. I was surprised by how snug the calves fit on my skinny legs.

I tried to pull them up as I high as possible to achieve a more comfortable fit, but the waistband reached to my bra line. Since I received them in a larger size, I rated these higher because I don't know if I would experience the same issues in the correct size, so I am giving them the benefit of doubt. Had these fit the same way in size small I would rate it at 3 stars.

I would recommend these for taller gals with long torsos and narrow calves.

Genuine Fred Howligans Dog Bandana, Large, Red I was excited to order these bandanas for my adult Corgi, Skip, and my new puppy I'm picking up soon! I got the red and the navy blue and even though there is no option to choose the size you want, based on other reviews, I was expecting the red to arrive in size small and this navy blue to be size medium/large. That is not the case. The blue one arrived first, in size small and unfortunately is too small for Skip. I can get the collar on him, but the ends barely overlap, leaving just enough space for the velcro to catch and the front triangle of material is laughably small on him.

I love the adorable print! There's images of squirrels, fire hydrants, balls, steaks and paw prints and cute sayings.. "Quite Fetching", "Ain't Too Proud To Beg". "Smell Ya later", You Gonna Eat That?", I'm All Ears!", "Gotta Run!", "Yo Dawg!" and "Shake On It". The product description claims that "the pattern is printed in reflective ink". I did not find this to be the case. The ink is silver and while it is shiny and kind of metallic, reflective it is not. This is not a deterrent for me, but may be for others.

I do like the velcro closure! I usually steer clear of dog bandanas because I don't like having to tie them on which makes the dog look silly with the two ends sticking out.. and I have rarely had luck finding a bandana that's the right size to my dog. I usually end up with a too large bandana (Corgi's a small-ish) that I fold in half into the standard triangle, tie it around his neck and then, not only does he have those "wings" sticking out from the tie, but he also is dwarfed by the size of the triangle in the front. My dogs don't need a bib or a necktie. LOL!

The sizing on this navy blue bandana (I have yet to receive the red one and am now quite curious to see what size shows up) is perfect for a smaller dog. I planned on Skip wearing this navy blue one, but it seems it will be given to my new Corgi puppy. The size small that I received will fit him properly and look right. I can only hope that I receive the red in a size medium/large so Skip gets to wear one too. If not, then the new pup will be off to a great start in the wardrobe department!

Bottom line... These are quite cute, very well made, the velcro is strong enough to hold through a round of scratching and seems as though it would hold during light play (we'll put that to the real test when our new puppy arrives!) and the size of the bandana itself (referring to the navy blue only) seems correct. But not being able to select the size you will receive is just shocking. It almost feels like a shot in the dark to order this - what size will I receive this time? That is not how anyone likes to shop and I'm surprised there is no size selection available for this reason.
text_fidelity_b: Genuine Fred Howligans Dog Bandana, Large, Red

text_fidelity_a:
Marcy Smith Cage Workout Machine Total Body Training Home Gym System with Linear Bearing Years ago, we bought the Marcy Diamond Elite Smith System after trying it in a local sports store. We liked the features, and the one at the store was awesome, with smooth motion on the cables, and since our place wasn't huge, this was as big as we could go for a piece of equipment. We brought it home; the visible parts were in good condition, and we put it together in a couple hours. It was about the quality you'd expect for the price, which means there were a couple welds that were off but nothing that was a problem.

Unfortunately the thing the cable runs through has a built-in plastic sleeve inside. This sleeve, which wasn't a separate part on its own, was torn inside. The more you'd use the cable, the harder it would be to pull through the sleeve as the flap would close, holding the cable and keeping it from moving freely. We called the manufacturer, and the woman I talked to was nice and had several suggestions, but when they didn't help, apparently the company was unable to just send us a replacement of the part housing the sleeve. I talked to another rep a couple days later, also very nice but unable to help. Ultimately we got rid of it and replaced it with a lat machine, since my main use for it was cable work.

If you get lucky and the plastic sleeve in yours isn't torn and everything else is good, it's a nice machine. Sure, it's not Inspire or Hoist, but it doesn't cost as much as their products do, either. Ours and the one at the store were good quality, lots of functions and it's fairly compact for what it is. The problem is you can't count on the manufacturer to help you out. We've had better luck with Impex for other products; for this particular part, two reps seemed helpless. And this is not something you want to take apart to ship back. But if you decide to take a shot, there's a lot to like about this machine as long as everything works.
text_fidelity_b: Marcy Smith Cage Workout Machine Total Body Training Home Gym System with Linear Bearing

text_fidelity_a:
Hydracentials Insulated Stainless Steel Metal Water Bottle with Straw Lid - Vacuum Insulated Water Bottles, Keeps Hot and Cold - Sports Canteen Bottle This is the smaller version of the second generation bottle. More about that in a minute. The reasons why I love this are the smaller size that fits in the beverage holder in my vehicle, and the improvements that were made when the second generation was released.

Improvements include the double wall construction that not only keeps this one (and the [[ASIN:B00LFPS0CY Hydracentials Sporty 25 Oz]] sibling) from sweating, but provides the insulation to keep drinks colder longer.

I can attest that the eight hour claim is absolutely true. To be sure it does not keep it ice cold that long, but it sure keeps it cold. I left mine in my car - with the insulation sock that shipped with mine - and it was cold hours later. This was in 95 degree weather, which would have turned a regular bottle of water hot. I am serious about that/ I did not test this without the additional insulating sock, but I am guessing that the water would have not gotten any warmer than cool without it.

Mine also came with a pair of straw cleaning brushes. I have not used those yet because I have found that soaking the top, straw and bottle in hot, soapy water, rinsing with a jet of clear water and air drying work perfectly.

Do note that this is NOT for hot liquids. It was not designed for them, and a hot liquid would probably ruin both the straw and the swivel piece to which it connects.

For me this is the ideal size, but click on the link to the 25 ounce model if you like your water supersized. Either way I think you'll be happy with one of these models because they are an improvement over others on the market that I have used, including this brand's original bottle.
text_fidelity_b: Hydracentials Insulated Stainless Steel Metal Water Bottle with Straw Lid - Vacuum Insulated Water Bottles, Keeps Hot and Cold - Sports Canteen Bottle

text_fidelity_a:
EBAT LED Lantern Recharged by solar panel+USB Cable for Travel, Picnic, Hiking, Yellow [[VIDEOID:7cace53d54dd11d9ca86d52ec20f0527]] If you ever go camping or if you live in an area where there are frequent power outages you understand the need for a good lantern. I have worked with several lanterns and while I have used some that are a little brighter or a little more compact, this one is a decent one that has some good features. Besides having a couple of operation modes, it is chargeable via solar energy.

This is a reasonably bright lantern but it is not blindingly bright like some others I have seen. This is a trade-off in my book. If you are expecting something that is bright enough to light a small camp area and allow you to read by it, this is a decent lamp. If you want something to light a 20'x20' room it is not strong enough to provide color recognition through the whole room.

This lantern has a rechargeable battery that can be removed and plugged in to the provided power adapter for recharging. It can also be opened up to expose a pair of solar panels so it can be charged up via solar power. There is something very important to understand about solar charging, though – using the solar panels to charge this lantern takes a lot longer than if plugging the pack in. I have not tried to completely charge the lantern via solar power but in my experience solar charging takes roughly 4 to 5 times longer. That said, if you do not have the option to plug in, the solar panel is a superb option.

This lantern seems to be solidly made and resistant to easy breakage. So, I believe it would survive a drop from a short distance, though I would hesitate to test this theory. The hook loop on top is plastic but it seems sturdy enough to handle frequent use and abuse.

This lantern has two operation modes. It has two brightnesses – dim and bright. The dim light is enough to light a hallway when carrying this lantern though it is not going to work for tromping through the woods. The bright setting is not actually all that bright but it is enough to see through a large room and make out everything in it, though it does not cast enough light to see colors clearly at more than 10' or so.

Overall, this is a decent little lantern. It seems to be made well and it can be charged by either a power adapter or solar power. Just keep in mind that it is not going to charge quickly if using the solar cells to charge it up.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: EBAT LED Lantern Recharged by solar panel+USB Cable for Travel, Picnic, Hiking, Yellow
